topic: The Geometric Intuition of Cramer's Rule
target_audience: University students or advanced high school students studying Linear Algebra

sections.title: The Algebra-Geometry Bridge
lecture_lines: Linear systems can be seen as vector combinations.
We seek scalars x and y for vector W.
W equals x times A plus y times B.
This transforms algebra into a geometric puzzle.
We must find how to reach the target destination.
animations: Show the 2x2 system of equations in white #FFFFFF.
Transform the equations into the vector equation xA + yB = W.
Draw vectors A (#00FF00) and B (#0000FF) on a 2D grid.
Draw target vector W (#FF0000) representing the drone's goal.
Show scaled vectors xA and yB forming a tip-to-tail sum to W.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Determinant as Area
lecture_lines: The determinant represents the area of a parallelogram.
Vectors A and B form our system's base area.
This area is the determinant of matrix AB.
animations: Display vectors A (#00FF00) and B (#0000FF) starting from the origin.
Create a parallelogram with A and B and fill with #888888.
Label the area of this parallelogram as det(A, B) in white #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Parallel-Transposition Trick
lecture_lines: Consider the parallelogram formed by vectors W and B.
Since yB is parallel to B, its area is zero.
Only the xA component contributes to this new area.
animations: Plot W (#FF0000) and B (#0000FF) on the 2D grid [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg].
Form a parallelogram using W and B with #FFAAAA fill.
Highlight the component of W parallel to B in yellow #FFFF00.

sections.title: The Ratio of Areas (Finding x)
lecture_lines: Replace vector A with target vector W.
The new area is x times the original area.
This geometric scaling reveals the value of x.
Thus, x is the ratio of these two areas.
This ratio is the essence of Cramer's Rule.
animations: Show Parallelogram(A, B) and Parallelogram(W, B) on a split screen.
Animate the transformation of Parallelogram(W, B) into Parallelogram(xA, B).
Scale Parallelogram(A, B) by x to match the area of Parallelogram(xA, B).
Display the ratio x = Area(W, B) / Area(A, B) in white #FFFFFF.
Reveal the determinant form x = det(W, B) / det(A, B) in white #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Symmetry for y and Higher Dimensions
lecture_lines: To find y, replace vector B with vector W.
The same area ratio logic applies to find y.
In 3D, we compare volumes of parallelepipeds instead.
animations: Replace B with W (#FF0000) in the original setup with A (#00FF00).
Display the formula y = det(A, W) / det(A, B) in white #FFFFFF.
Show a 3D volume (parallelepiped) briefly to generalize to 3D.

sections.title: Summary and the 'Cramer Formula'
lecture_lines: Cramer's Rule links geometric areas to algebraic solutions.
The solution exists if the base area is non-zero.
This formula works for any number of dimensions.
Algebra and geometry unite in this elegant solution.
Understanding this bridge simplifies complex linear systems.
animations: Present the general Cramer's Rule formula for xi in white #FFFFFF.
Flash the denominator det(A) in red #FF0000 to show singularity.
